tickers.notes: Revenue growth negative last 2 quarters (-1.6%, -22.7% YoY); PE 34.8 / EV-EBITDA 108 is rich even for AAPL. FCF and trend still strong.
Broadly healthy. Operating margin has drifted down ~4pts over 4 quarters even as gross margin ticked up; FCF choppy (one quarter at $5.9B vs $15-26B range) but not concerning yet.

Cleanest sheet of the test set. EPS growth of only 2.9% looks low relative to 17.9% revenue growth — worth a closer look on margin/share-count effects in a real run, not flagged red on this data alone.

FCF and D/E read red mechanically (FCF swings -$211B to +$120B quarter to quarter, D/E 3.3x, net-debt/EBITDA 31x) but this is normal for a bank's balance sheet, not a distress signal — checklist items 6-7 are built for non-financials and need sector context for banks. Fundamentals (revenue, margin, EPS growth) all green; valuation cheap at 10.8x PE.

Standout divergence: fundamentals improving fast (revenue +18%, EPS +42%, margins expanding) but price down ~16% over 3 months vs SPY +2.9%, D/E 2.3x, PE 34x. Worth a real look — either the market is pricing in something the trailing financials don't show yet, or this is a name getting cheaper while getting better.
